name: ai-ready
description: Audit AI-agent readiness, apply reviewed guidance improvements, and run unattended maker/checker loops (loop-run/build/lessons) in Codex. v0.8.7+: inject_lazy_load_index drops auto-table rows whose document is already linked from the user section — the root CLAUDE.md is always-loaded, so a doc listed in both the hand-written and the generated table costs its duplicate every session (12 rows / ~1,558 chars in one repo). Link targets are compared with trailing slashes normalized, only a row whose every target is already covered is dropped, and when all detected docs are covered the auto block renders a one-line note instead of an empty table — automating what previously needed hand-maintained config.override_hardcoded entries. v0.8.8+: the root `## 모듈 맵` stub listing length is config-driven — `module_map.root_stub_limit` (default 10, unchanged); 0 keeps only the catalog link and drops the per-module excerpt. The root doc is always-loaded and each module's one-line summary already lives in its own CLAUDE.md (auto-loaded when that module is opened), so the excerpt is duplicate context in repos that link enough paths elsewhere (~1,800 chars in one repo). Because audit's "root doc references 3+ module/doc paths" rule counts that listing as a reference source in some repos, the default is unchanged and setting 0 prints a notice instead of silently losing points. Bad values (negative, bool, non-int) fall back to the default rather than breaking generation.

interface.shortDescription: Audit and safely improve AI-agent guidance.
interface.longDescription: Assess a repository's AI-agent readiness, prepare reviewed guidance improvements, and check documentation freshness without Claude-only hooks.
defaultPrompt: Audit this repository for AI-agent readiness.
Plan the approved improvements from the latest AI-Ready audit.
Check whether this repository's guidance documents are stale.
Use loop-run to converge this change to a PASS verdict.
Use loop-build to build out this approved design across phases.
